entries.text:
Both commits matched up correctly by sha and timestamp, with the working tree untouched. I'm now counting back through my action sequence since the last commit to verify the gap of six actions lines up with what actually happened—checking sqlite and ledger work that followed the mapping request.

Turning to the UI layer, I'm sketching out the API shape: a ledger group with a range endpoint that returns commits or a failure, plus a repos endpoint pulling from stored projects. For the web side, I'm planning a LedgerPage route with a repo selector, range input, and expandable commit cards showing sha, subject, thread title, and match status—reusing the action tree rendering logic from ActionView by extracting it into a shared HistoryTree component rather than rendering each commit as a full heavy ThreadView.

I'm now weighing how to represent each commit as a synthetic turn within that shared tree view—inserting a marker message for the commit versus reclassifying the original user messages, which risks misrepresenting the data. I'm considering whether to add an optional alternate turn-splitting parameter to the tree builder, or introduce a new message/event type for commits, but that would ripple into the schema, so I'm leaning toward the simplest approach that avoids touching the domain model.

I'll skip the combined swimlane for now and add an `embedded` prop to ActionView that suppresses the header, toolbar, swimlane, and title changes, leaving just the tree rendered. For the ledger page, I'll build commit cards with a sha chip, subject, time, thread match info, and a collapsible body embedding ActionView — adjusting its props to accept either a `view` or `artifact` alongside `embedded`.

I need to construct a ThreadView from each LedgerEntry's commit data (title, timestamps, action count) plus entries and labels, default commits to expanded, and populate the repo dropdown from ledger projects while allowing manual path entry. I'll also add a link from the sessions page over to the ledger view.

I'm handling hash-based routing like `#/ledger?repo=...&range=...` and making sure the main router recognizes paths starting with `#/ledger`, plus returning a 400 error for bad range parameters. Now let me write the implementation.



Both commits were confirmed and logged to `agent-ledger` (commit `2707c31`) without touching the code branch. Now I'll build a ledger viewer page where you select a repo and range to see the agent work behind each commit, reusing the action viewer embedded per commit.

entries.text:
The output works and shows actions per commit, but I notice some segments include leading turns with zero actions—just discussion before the first real action. I should consider trimming those leading no-action turns while still preserving useful context, since the user wants the agent's actions per commit, not noise.

I'm refining the segment boundary logic: find the last user message at or before the first action index, and prepend it so the segment shows meaningful context even when it starts mid-turn. I'm weighing whether to include the earlier non-action notes in between, deciding it's acceptable to drop full turns lacking actions to keep segments clean.

I'm tracing through a specific test case where splitting at a commit produces two turns, confirming the kept segment gets the original prompt prepended even though it duplicates across segments, then updating the test's expected entry ids to match this new behavior.

The export-only button display and matched-by labels (sha/time) look correct already, so I'll go ahead and implement the segmentFor change now.



The per-commit viewer works well overall, but I spotted two segmentation issues to fix: leading discussion-only turns (no actions) should be dropped from a segment's start, and segments starting mid-turn should still show the original prompt instead of "no prompt."
